topics.label: Introduction to cancer therapy lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and defines its primary learning objectives regarding cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, detailing their mechanisms, systemic toxicities, and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor-specific vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain strategies that target intrinsic vulnerabilities of cancer cells, including hormone receptors, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair pathways through synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine oncogene addiction and small-molecule kinase inhibitors, detailing their structural design, therapeutic applications, and mechanisms of acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss antibody-based therapeutic approaches, including receptor blockade, immune-mediated cytotoxicity, and targeted delivery of cytotoxic drugs.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular immune responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore tumor immune surveillance and cellular immunotherapies, focusing on checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific T-cell engagers, and chimeric antigen receptor T cells.

topics.label: Overarching challenges, progress, and future perspectives in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader trajectory of cancer treatment, synthesizing major clinical challenges, historical improvements in survival, and emerging future strategies.
